newsitem.title: USA: KC Power seen approving $32/shr Western bid.
newsitem.headline: KC Power seen approving $32/shr Western bid.

text.p: Kansas City Power and Light Co directors are expected to approve a sweetened takeover bid of $32 a share from Western Resources Inc at a meeting to be held as early as today, sources close to the situation said.
The $2 billion stock-swap would be the first successful hostile takeover among U.S. utilities.
Western raised its bid from $31 a share after long negotiations, the sources said. Western launched its hostile offer for KCP&L last April with a bid of $28 a share.

KCP&L's surrender would end a 10-month battle that saw the company's friendly merger pact with UtiliCorp United Inc fall apart after the less lucrative offer was rejected by KCP&L shareholders in September.
Spokeswomen for Western and KCP&L today declined comment, but a source close to the situation said, "They have been talking for a long time and I think this is it," referring to the KCP&L board vote.
Analysts have said that if the merger goes through, it will create a Midwestern electric and natural gas powerhouse better poised to compete as the U.S. utility business is deregulated.
The new company would operate primarily in Kansas, Missouri and Oklahoma and have annual revenue of almost $3 billion.
The sources confirmed a New York Times report that Western's board approved the KCP&L deal earlier this week.
Western still has outstanding a $3.5 billion hostile bid for security company ADT Ltd, in which it already owns a 27.1 percent stake.
